Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Virtual offices are acceptable for initial correspondence and registered address purposes, provided the notarial deed records the physical address of management or principal establishment if different. For a franchise licensing and syrup supply-chain entity, a purely virtual office without local management, personnel, books, or operational nexus is unacceptable for VAT registration, economic-substance expectations, and banking. It may be treated as a 'letterbox' and trigger tax anti-abuse rules, permanent establishment exposure, or denial of treaty benefits.

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind; cash capital must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution or Banco de España blocked account prior to deed execution.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate issued by a qualified technician and approved by the local fire service or Ayuntamiento; structural load inspection for equipment and storage areas; workplace health and safety assessment under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including emergency evacuation plans.

Paid-in capital rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind; cash capital must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution or Banco de España blocked account prior to deed execution.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica, https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; Madrid Central Office, Calle Infanta Mercedes 37.

E-government filing portal

For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), the definitive NIF is granted by AEAT upon incorporation after filing Form 030 (prior declaration) and Form 036 (census filing). The SL must register in the Censo de Empresarios before beginning any economic activity and will be issued a NIF with the 'ES' VAT prefix (NIF-IVA). Foreign non-resident entities with no permanent establishment that engage in taxable Spanish supplies must file Form 036 to obtain a non-resident Spanish NIF and, if established outside the EU/EEA, appoint a tax representative recognized by AEAT (Art. 164.Dos Ley 37/1992). Registration is immediate and unconditional; there is no turnover threshold that exempts the SL from obtaining a NIF. All applications are submitted electronically using a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN through the AEAT portal.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Spanish SL is a resident company subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income. No pass-through treatment is available to a standard SL. Territorial Scope: tax-resident entities are taxed on worldwide income with double-tax relief; non-resident entities are taxed only on Spanish-source income. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none at the national level; a limited special ZEC regime applies in the Canary Islands, not applicable to a mainland SL franchise business. — For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), the definitive NIF is granted by AEAT upon incorporation after filing Form 030 (prior declaration) and Form 036 (census filing). The SL must register in the Censo de Empresarios before beginning any economic activity and will be issued a NIF with the 'ES' VAT prefix (NIF-IVA). Foreign non-resident entities with no permanent establishment that engage in taxable Spanish supplies must file Form 036 to obtain a non-resident Spanish NIF and, if established outside the EU/EEA, appoint a tax representative recognized by AEAT (Art. 164.Dos Ley 37/1992). Registration is immediate and unconditional; there is no turnover threshold that exempts the SL from obtaining a NIF. All applications are submitted electronically using a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN through the AEAT portal.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — the Spanish SL is a resident company subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income. No pass-through treatment is available to a standard SL. Territorial Scope: tax-resident entities are taxed on worldwide income with double-tax relief; non-resident entities are taxed only on Spanish-source income. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none at the national level; a limited special ZEC regime applies in the Canary Islands, not applicable to a mainland SL franchise business.

Available election forms

No IRS-style check-the-box election exists in Spain. Available elections relevant to this SL: (1) consolidated tax group election under Arts. 62–75 LIS (parent owns ≥75%, group treated as one taxpayer); (2) simplified VAT regime (régimen simplificado) for enumerated retail/manufacturing activities with turnover up to EUR 250,000; (3) VAT cash-accounting scheme (criterio de caja) for SMEs with turnover up to EUR 2,000,000; (4) Patent Box election under Art. 23 LIS permitting a reduced effective rate on qualifying franchise/IP income; (5) hybrid-mismatch neutrality elections required by ATAD, applicable to franchise/royalty cross-border structures.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

Zero turnover threshold: every taxable person, including the ES_SL, must register before carrying out business activity. For small-business simplified VAT regime: EUR 250,000 annual turnover in eligible activities (EUR 125,000 for agriculture). For EU remote sellers: EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold in Spain triggers registration unless the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) is used.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero-rating applies under Art. 21 LIVA to exports of tangible goods physically leaving the EU (bubble-tea syrups, equipment, packaging) provided the exporter is the consignor and holds documentary evidence of actual exit. Franchise royalties and distribution services supplied by the Spanish SL to a foreign franchisee are treated as B2B services 'effectively used and exploited' outside Spain and are outside the scope of VAT/reverse-charged in the customer's jurisdiction; intra-EU supplies of goods to a VAT-registered franchisee are zero-rated (Art. 25 LIVA) with the customer's valid VAT ID. Zero-rating is claimable only for the exact quantity that customs records prove to have left Spain/EU territory.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUI/SAD) filed through the Spanish DUEx customs application showing the ES_SL as exporter
  • Transport document of exit: Sea Bill of Lading, CMR (international road consignment note), or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
  • Commercial invoice quoting Incoterms and stating the export sale price
  • Franchisee tax identification evidence (VAT registration certificate or foreign tax ID) for services and intra-EU dispatches
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103) or bank statement evidencing FX repatriation of export proceeds
  • Customs exit certificate 'justificante de salida' issued by the office of departure or destination

Spain imposes B2B e-invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece (Ley 18/2022); invoices must be issued/transmitted in structured XML via interoperable private platforms. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA) mandates near-real-time transmission of VAT invoice records to AEAT for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,000,000, and is obligatory for certain e-commerce operators; SII filings use Web Services/API with an XML schema (4.2) and a 4-day submission period. Under VeriFactu (RD 1007/2023), all billing software must produce verifiable invoices bearing a QR code and hash-chain digital fingerprint; the issuance timestamp and invoice data must be legally retained and made accessible to AEAT. Real-time per-invoice fiscal clearance is not generally required outside the SII framework, but non-SII taxpayers must maintain a certified billing system capable of instant AEAT inspection.

AEAT applies strict documentary audits using DUEx/ENS/EXS customs data cross-checks. Missing or fraudulent export proof retroactively converts zero-rated invoices into VAT-liable sales, triggering repayment of unused input VAT refunded, 5% annual late interest, and the recargo de apremio (5–20% late-payment surcharge). A false zero-rating claim is an infracción tributaria grave under Art. 191 LGT with penalties of 50–150% of the VAT unpaid. Forgery or simulation of export documentation with amount above EUR 120,000 constitutes a criminal tax offence under Art. 305 Código Penal, imprisonment of 2–6 years and fines of up to six times the tax amount. Additionally, if export proceeds are not repatriated to a Spanish account within 180 days, AEAT may presume disinvestment, disallow the export VAT refund, and impose exchange-control civil penalties.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. Spain has no general exchange-control approval requirement for foreign investment, capital contributions, intercompany loans, dividends, royalties, or trade payments. Capital movements remain subject to anti-money-laundering controls, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner verification, tax documentation, statistical reporting, and applicable foreign-investment declarations. Dividend and royalty remittances may be subject to Spanish withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, or another statutory exemption. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, corporate approvals, tax residence certificates, and proof of tax compliance before processing remittances.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to Banco de España, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal repatriation deadline. Export proceeds may generally remain in euro or foreign-currency accounts and may be converted at the company's discretion. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs records, transport evidence, contracts, and payment records, and must satisfy bank transaction-monitoring and applicable statistical-reporting obligations. Cash or bearer negotiable instruments transported into or out of the European Union at amounts of EUR 10,000 or more require a customs declaration; intra-EU movements may be subject to Spanish declaration requirements where applicable.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange rules are principally governed by European Union law and Spanish financial legislation.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium to High for euro-denominated payments, collections, virtual IBANs, card acquiring, and treasury interfaces where the provider is authorized by an EU or EEA competent authority and lawfully passported or established in Spain. A non-EU offshore digital EMI cannot provide regulated payment services to the Spanish company on a cross-border basis without an appropriate EU authorization, passport, Spanish establishment, or legally valid agent arrangement. EMI funds are safeguarded and are not equivalent to deposits; deposit-guarantee protection may not apply. Fintech onboarding does not eliminate Spanish AML, beneficial-owner, tax, sanctions, payment-purpose, or source-of-funds requirements.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain or nominee arrangement.

Root cause: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain or nominee arrangement.

Defense evidence: Certified constitutional documents; current commercial-register extracts; complete ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address; director appointment evidence; beneficial-owner declaration; notarized powers of attorney; and, where relevant, apostille, legalization, and sworn Spanish translation.
New Spanish SL with no operating history, limited local substance, or expected international royalty and supply-chain payments.

Root cause: New Spanish SL with no operating history, limited local substance, or expected international royalty and supply-chain payments.

Defense evidence: Executed business plan; franchise agreements; supplier and logistics contracts; lease or registered-office evidence; staffing plan; projected monthly cash flows; expected countries, currencies, counterparties, and transaction volumes; board-approved treasury policy; and evidence of Spanish commercial activity.
Inbound capital from a third-party account, high-risk jurisdiction, cryptocurrency source, or unexplained foreign shareholder loan.

Root cause: Inbound capital from a third-party account, high-risk jurisdiction, cryptocurrency source, or unexplained foreign shareholder loan.

Defense evidence: Bank statements tracing the source of funds; audited or filed financial statements of the funding entity; shareholder resolutions; capital-increase or loan agreements; tax-residence certificates; proof of beneficial ownership; financing-purpose memorandum; sanctions screening; and independent evidence of the original wealth source.
Royalty, management-fee, or syrup-supply payments to related parties outside Spain.

Root cause: Royalty, management-fee, or syrup-supply payments to related parties outside Spain.

Defense evidence: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing analysis; invoices; proof of services or delivery; customs and transport records; intellectual-property ownership evidence; withholding-tax analysis; treaty or EU exemption documentation; economic-beneficiary confirmation; and accounting reconciliation.
Unusual cash intensity, rapid pass-through flows, refunds, chargebacks, or POS collections inconsistent with the declared bubble-tea franchise model.

Root cause: Unusual cash intensity, rapid pass-through flows, refunds, chargebacks, or POS collections inconsistent with the declared bubble-tea franchise model.

Defense evidence: POS and acquiring contracts; store-level sales forecasts; cash-handling procedures; daily reconciliation reports; merchant statements; refund and chargeback policy; point-of-sale controls; franchisee screening files; inventory records; and management explanations for material variances.
Incomplete tax identification, mismatch between corporate records and bank application, or inability to verify Spanish operating address.

Root cause: Incomplete tax identification, mismatch between corporate records and bank application, or inability to verify Spanish operating address.

Defense evidence: NIF certificate; deed of incorporation; Mercantile Registry extract; registered-office evidence; lease or utility documentation; corporate tax registration; director and shareholder identification; and a consistency memorandum reconciling all legal names, addresses, ownership percentages, and business activities.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity through a regulated bank using a transfer from an account held by the actual shareholder or funding entity, with an accurate payment narrative identifying equity subscription, share capital increase, or shareholder loan. For a capital increase, obtain the bank's capital-contribution certificate, execute the notarial deed, and register the increase with the Mercantile Registry. Maintain shareholder resolutions, subscription documents, source-of-funds evidence, and beneficial-owner records. Foreign direct investment and statistical filings may be required depending on investor, amount, sector, ownership, and transaction characteristics; filings should be assessed under Spanish foreign-investment reporting rules and Banco de España statistical requirements. Spanish banks may use internal purpose codes rather than a universal statutory payment-code system. Do not split transfers to avoid controls, and ensure the remitter, beneficiary, amount, currency, invoice or agreement, and tax treatment are consistent.Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. Provide invoice, purchase order, contract, customs documentation where relevant, beneficiary ownership information, and sanctions-screening data. For imported syrups, packaging, equipment, or franchise-related goods, use documentary collections or a commercial letter of credit where counterparty or jurisdiction risk warrants enhanced control. A commercial LC should specify issuing and confirming banks, documentary conditions, Incoterms, shipment documents, inspection requirements, discrepancy rules, applicable UCP 600 or other agreed rules, currency, tenor, and charges. Royalty and service payments require contract, invoice, beneficial-recipient, transfer-pricing, and withholding-tax support. Banks may apply enhanced review to payments involving sanctioned, high-risk, or restricted jurisdictions.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank for documented forecast or committed exposures, subject to suitability, confirmations, collateral, accounting, and applicable MiFID II and EMIR requirements.Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility, where offered by an appropriately regulated counterparty and used for a genuine commercial exposure; settlement, documentation, reporting, and counterparty-risk controls are required.Plain-vanilla currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring intercompany funding or longer-term currency mismatches, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, valuation, collateral, EMIR reporting, and board-approved risk limits.Foreign-exchange options or collars for documented commercial exposures, provided the structure is proportionate, understood by management, and not used for speculative trading.Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, currency clauses in franchise and supply contracts, and centralized treasury netting where legally and operationally documented.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium to High for euro-denominated payments, collections, virtual IBANs, card acquiring, and treasury interfaces where the provider is authorized by an EU or EEA competent authority and lawfully passported or established in Spain. A non-EU offshore digital EMI cannot provide regulated payment services to the Spanish company on a cross-border basis without an appropriate EU authorization, passport, Spanish establishment, or legally valid agent arrangement. EMI funds are safeguarded and are not equivalent to deposits; deposit-guarantee protection may not apply. Fintech onboarding does not eliminate Spanish AML, beneficial-owner, tax, sanctions, payment-purpose, or source-of-funds requirements.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Deposit of Annual Accounts ('Depósito de Cuentas Anuales') comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, directors' report, and audit report if applicable Approval at the Ordinary General Meeting within 6 months of fiscal year-end and deposit within 1 month of approval; outer deadline 30 July for a calendar-year company $130 USD Late filing penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 60,000 per fiscal year under Art. 283 LSC; closure of the Mercantile Registry filing window ('cierre registral') for all other deeds or registrations until deposited; persistent non-filing for 3 or more consecutive years may trigger aggravated sanctions and administrative strike-off.

Approval at the Ordinary General Meeting within 6 months of fiscal year-end and deposit within 1 month of approval; outer deadline 30 July for a calendar-year company

Late filing penalties

Late filing penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 60,000 per fiscal year under Art. 283 LSC; closure of the Mercantile Registry filing window ('cierre registral') for all other deeds or registrations until deposited; persistent non-filing for 3 or more consecutive years may trigger aggravated sanctions and administrative strike-off.

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: Independent statutory audit is mandatory for a Spanish SL when, on two consecutive balance-sheet dates, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total assets greater than EUR 4,000,000; annual net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory if the general meeting resolves it at the request of shareholders holding 5% of the share capital, or when the company is part of a group required to produce consolidated audited accounts.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax Act (IRNR), unless reduced by treaty or eliminated under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. 0% applies for a qualifying EU/EEA parent company holding at least 10% of the Spanish SL for at least one year, with anti-abuse substance verification.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Twenty-five days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; for a fiscal year ending 31 December, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Header (Cabecera Modelo 200) Taxpayer identification: NIF, legal name, registered address, tax year start/end, corporate form (SL), accounting framework, ISIC/NAICS business code. Non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners must be identified; the Spanish SL is the filing entity and must maintain an in-country tax representative if administrative notifications are required. Late filing surcharge (LGT art. 27): 1% per calendar month of delay up to 12 months, plus late-payment interest; after 12 months the surcharge is 15% plus late-payment interest. Penalty for non-filing or incomplete return (LGT art. 198): EUR 200 per data omission, minimum EUR 1,500. If underpayment is detected, penalty of 50%-150% of the amount underpaid. Late payment interest is currently 5% per annum in 2025 or as updated by the PGEAct.
Accounting result (Resultado contable del ejercicio) Book profit or loss before corporate tax under Spanish GAAP, including revenue from franchise royalties, syrup supply sales, POS receipts, and operating expenses. Foreign parent accounting adjustments must be reconciled to Spanish GAAP; non-resident related-party transactions must be fully recorded and reconciled with the TP policy. Late filing surcharge (LGT art. 27): 1% per calendar month of delay up to 12 months, plus late-payment interest; after 12 months the surcharge is 15% plus late-payment interest. Penalty for non-filing or incomplete return (LGT art. 198): EUR 200 per data omission, minimum EUR 1,500. If underpayment is detected, penalty of 50%-150% of the amount underpaid. Late payment interest is currently 5% per annum in 2025 or as updated by the PGEAct.
Taxable base and adjustments (Base imponible y correcciones) Permanent and temporary differences, transfer pricing adjustments, compensation of prior tax losses, reserve deductions, and other corrections resulting in the final taxable base. Cross-border royalty and service payments from the SL to a non-resident affiliate must be arm's length; documentation of the economic substance of the non-resident recipient must be retained in Spain. Late filing surcharge (LGT art. 27): 1% per calendar month of delay up to 12 months, plus late-payment interest; after 12 months the surcharge is 15% plus late-payment interest. Penalty for non-filing or incomplete return (LGT art. 198): EUR 200 per data omission, minimum EUR 1,500. If underpayment is detected, penalty of 50%-150% of the amount underpaid. Late payment interest is currently 5% per annum in 2025 or as updated by the PGEAct.
Tax liability and payment (Cuota íntegra, cuota líquida y deuda tributaria) Application of 25% statutory rate, tax credits, withholdings, quarterly prepayments already made, and final amount due or refundable. Withholding on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents must be declared separately via Modelo 216; treaty relief or EU Directive exemptions require prior filing of Modelo 210 for refund. Late filing surcharge (LGT art. 27): 1% per calendar month of delay up to 12 months, plus late-payment interest; after 12 months the surcharge is 15% plus late-payment interest. Penalty for non-filing or incomplete return (LGT art. 198): EUR 200 per data omission, minimum EUR 1,500. If underpayment is detected, penalty of 50%-150% of the amount underpaid. Late payment interest is currently 5% per annum in 2025 or as updated by the PGEAct.
Related-party operations Annex / Modelo 232 trigger Disclosure of controlled transactions with related persons: franchise licence, management fees, financing, and goods supply; value, method used, and final transfer price. A foreign parent or sister company receiving Spanish royalties must furnish a Tax Residence Certificate; when thresholds exceed EUR 250,000 or turnover exceeds EUR 10 million, Modelo 232 must be filed. Late filing surcharge (LGT art. 27): 1% per calendar month of delay up to 12 months, plus late-payment interest; after 12 months the surcharge is 15% plus late-payment interest. Penalty for non-filing or incomplete return (LGT art. 198): EUR 200 per data omission, minimum EUR 1,500. If underpayment is detected, penalty of 50%-150% of the amount underpaid. Late payment interest is currently 5% per annum in 2025 or as updated by the PGEAct.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File / Modelo 232 disclosure is mandatory when (a) net turnover equals or exceeds EUR 10 million, or (b) the aggregate amount of related-party transactions in the tax period exceeds EUR 250,000. Master File is required when consolidated group turnover of the ultimate parent equals or exceeds EUR 50 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain applies substance requirements through the GAAR (art. 15 LGT), CFC rules, and TP anti-abuse provisions. A Spanish SL receiving franchise royalties or paying fees to a foreign affiliate must show real local business functions, staff and premises. A mailbox company with artificial arrangements may be recharacterized, deductions may be denied, and treaty benefits may be refused under the Principal Purpose Test.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (Criminal Fraud - Art. 305 Criminal Code)

Statutory sanction: Imprisonment of 1 to 4 years, plus a fine ranging from the amount defrauded to six times that amount. If the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 600,000 or the offence is committed through interposed persons, imprisonment extends to 2-6 years and the fine is higher.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly order, consent to, or conceal the fraud are criminally liable as perpetrators. Civil liability may pierce the corporate veil under LGT Art. 42.1(a) and 42.2, making directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, interest and penalties. Travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification from management may be imposed during criminal proceedings.
Wholly Artificial Arrangement / Shell Company Abuse

Statutory sanction: GAAR recharacterisation with upward transfer pricing adjustments, denial of royalty and interest deductions, imposition of the standard 25% tax plus late-payment interest, and penalties of 50% to 150% of the undercharged tax under LGT Arts. 191-193. Failure to comply with documentation requirements triggers additional fixed penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors who intentionally created the artificial structure to evade tax are jointly liable for the hidden tax debt; in criminal cases, imprisonment applies for fraud over EUR 120,000. Travel bans and corporate veil piercing are available under LGT Art. 42.2.
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Controlled Transaction Filing Failure

Statutory sanction: Tax administration may adjust the taxable base to arm's length and issue a collection assessment. Late payment interest accrues, and penalties of up to 50% of the undercharged tax apply if the adjustment is treated as wrongful underreporting. Formal non-compliance with TP documentation carries fixed penalties under LGT Art. 198 (EUR 200 per omitted data item, minimum EUR 1,500).

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly signed or approved false intercompany contracts and invoices can be held personally liable for the adjusted tax, interest and penalties. Where the TP adjustment arises from deliberate fraud, criminal liability under Art. 305 Criminal Code follows with imprisonment and travel bans.
Anti-Money Laundering / Beneficial Ownership Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: Under Law 10/2010 on Money Laundering Prevention: minor infringement, fine up to EUR 60,000; serious infringement, fine up to EUR 1.5 million; very serious infringement, fine up to EUR 10 million plus prohibition from operating in the sector for up to five years. If laundering is criminalised under Art. 301 Criminal Code, imprisonment ranges from 1 to 6 years and fines up to six times the laundered value.

Director personal liability: Directors are personally liable where they knowingly failed to adopt AML/CTF procedures or consented to laundering. Criminal sanctions can be imposed directly on the director, including imprisonment, travel bans, asset freezes and disqualification from holding administrative positions in Spanish companies.
